recipes.name: Grilled Pheasant Poppers
ingredients_raw: 6 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 20 minutes

steps.text: Cut pheasant breast into 36 pieces and place into a large bowl. Pour liquid from jalapeño peppers over pheasant; stir and marinate at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.
Drain marinade from pheasant and discard. Place a jalapeño pepper slice on each piece of pheasant breast and wrap with 1/3 of a bacon strip. Skewer 6 bacon-wrapped pheasant pieces onto each skewer.
Cook on the preheated grill, turning frequently, until bacon is crispy, 15 to 20 minutes. Remove pheasant pieces from the skewers and insert a toothpick into each piece to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Pheasant Poppers
raw_recipe.description: These grilled pheasant poppers are easy to make with jalapeño peppers and bacon for a spicy, crisp, and delicious appetizer that always gets rave reviews.

review.reviewBody: Awsome! We soaked the pheasant in buttermilk overnight to get rid of the gamey taste. Very good super bowl appetizer!

I first made this following the recipe, except I brined the breasts first. The second time, I used jalapeño peppers to hold the strips of breast. Cut the jalapeños in half, removed the seeds and white veins. Next I place a layer of cream cheese, then the breast and wrapped in bacon. Because of the larger size I used 2 skewers, 4 popper per the set of skewers. Sorry I didn’t take a picture but they were great! You could probably forgo the skewers all together and use toothpicks on each popper to hold the bacon in place.

Add a little piece of cheese (of your preference). If you want to, a pinch of garlic can also add some extra flavor to the bites. I make these every fall during pheasant season! One of the benefits of living in South Dakota! Next time I'm going to make these in my smoker, instead of the usual grill. I'll try to remember to update this comment with how it turned out!

Our family makes these all the time!! We maranate the pheasant over night in italian dressing, put them together and just through them under the broiler for about 5 minutes. This insures that the pheasant isn't over cooked and we like our bacon a little on the rare side. We don't have a family event without them!!
We also brush it with some teriyaki sauce before grilling, which is awesome. And you can make it with duck also. Even people who "hate duck" will eat it. Works well broiled in the oven too.
We do this on the Traeger using dove and add a little dab of cream cheese in the middle. I'm sure its just as good with pheasant! YUMMY!

Wow, these are great. My husband hunts but I hate eating pheasant so we usually give it away. This is the best pheasant dish I've had. I took it to a NYE party and people really loved them! I live in MN so grilling is tough in the winter... I just baked them and they turned out perfect!

Took this to a christmas party and went over well, but I did do something a little different. Since my crew and I do not like things really hot and this was on the hot side. I added some teriyaki sauce to the poppers once they were cooked. It had a great flavor and still had enough heat.

These were great! I am making them again tomorrow, my pheasant is soaking in milk to remove the gamey taste as we speak. Im thinking of making shish kabobs out of them this time for a meal instead of an appetizer. Also going to try the broiler as the grill is put away for the winter.
These are so good! Be sure to use jarred jalopenos, not the canned ones for nachos. We learned the hard way that those are way to big and much hotter!
These are amazing! I usually am not a big fan of game bird, but these are unbelievable! We used pickled jalapenos (Mrs Renfros) Amazing! Highly recomended!
Made this exactly as written and it was great! Served it to friends who aren't pheasant hunters or eaters and they loved it. I will definitely make this again!
Excellent! This was easy enough - even for a non-detailed woman!!
Great the best way to make pheasant. I add a like Worcester sauce and brown sugar on them. Quality of bacon really makes it better, I like the neater bacon.
Efing amazing :)
These are so great! We've made them many times and they are always a huge hit. We can't ever make enough of them!
Be careful to get the bacon fully cooked!

I finally found a way to cook pheasant that I like, and come back for more. I spread a little cream cheese on the end before eating to push the poppers into the "next dimension." Pheasant season is over, so we'll have to make due with chicken poppers until next year.
VERY SIMPLE AND EASY TO PREPARE RECIPE, MAKES FOR A GREAT BBQ APPETIZER
i made these with fresh peppers from my garden and added a some cheddar cheese. they were fantastic!
